author: research agent A-EXT
scope_note: Exteriors of dwellings and shops for tiers 1-3 (minka, machiya, nagaya, shop fronts, hatago, tea houses, family kura). Parts only: the architect (C) assembles buildings from them. Out of scope (see BUILD_LIST.md, Later): temples/shrines, government/castle, street dressing, gardens/site sets, interiors.

entries.name: Roof forms and footprint rules (kirizuma / yosemune / irimoya)

entries.period_evidence: Kitamura house 1687, yosemune thatch [E01]; Kiyomiya late 17th c. yosemune thatch [E01]; Ito late 17th-early 18th c. irimoya thatch [E01]; Hirose late 17th c. kirizuma thatch [x08]; Sasaki 1731/32 yosemune thatch with stone-weighted board eaves [E02]; Ioka late 17th-early 18th c. kirizuma sangawara machiya [E03]; tile banned in Edo 1657 except storehouses, encouraged 1720 [E09]

refs.shows: Sasaki house 1732: thatch with board pent eave
Ioka machiya: kirizuma sangawara, gable pent roof
roadside tea house: thatch kirizuma + board pents

grid_m.value: 1.820 ken / 0.910 half-ken; footprints are unions of ken rectangles

pitch_ishioki_sun.value: 3-3.5 (16.7-19.3 deg); steeper and the stones slide

pitch_thatch_deg.value: 45 (50-60 only gassho, not on our map)

main_span_townhouse_ken.value: <=3 between main-roof walls (Edo townsmen rule 1668); extra depth by lean-to

plan_examples_m.value: Kitamura 15.6x8.9; Kiyomiya 13.6x8.2; Ito 16.4x9.1; Sasaki 24.7x10.0; Ioka 7.9 wide x 12.7 deep; Misawa 13.6x12.7

eave line = keta top outer edge
ridge line centred on the span
kawara columns 0.260 m = 7 per ken, so a column edge lands on every ken line
lean-to (geya/hisashi) roofs attach below the main eave at a wall line
